title: Ines and the Cipher
premise: Estate lawyer Petra Marchetti is hired to probate a will for a woman who, according to every record, died thirty years ago — and the only witness to its signing turns up murdered, wearing clothes taken from Petra's own closet. As Petra investigates, they discover the will is a coded confession to a decades-old crime committed by the town's founding family, and that Petra's own late mother was one of the conspirators who bought her survival with silence. When the trial of the chief suspect begins, Petra must choose between protecting their name and exposing a cipher that names every survivor — including themselves, as the beneficiary of stolen money. In the end, Petra reads the decoded will aloud in court, forfeiting their inheritance and, at last, finding belonging in truth rather than silence.
about_author: Freya Voss spent fifteen years as a probate clerk in a small coastal town before turning to fiction, and her mysteries are known for their forensic attention to paperwork and inheritance law. She lives in a converted notary's office with an ill-tempered cat named Codicil.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra Marchetti, a lawyer who prides herself on closing every case, is handed a will signed by Elena Varga — a woman whose death certificate is thirty years old. The document is written partly in cipher. Petra accepts the case against her better judgment, unsettled by how much the testator seemed to know about her. Emotional beat: professional pride masking a flicker of dread.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The will's sole witness, archivist Tomas Reiner, is found strangled in his office — dressed in clothes stolen from Petra's own closet, making her the prime suspect. The detective, Inspector Halloran, is polite but unconvinced by her alibi. Petra realizes someone is framing her with intimate knowledge of her life. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: POV Petra, with an interpolated letter from Elena. Petra digs into the night Elena Varga supposedly died: a fire at the Aldous estate, four survivors, four identical statements. Every alibi is airtight — too airtight, rehearsed. Petra's mother's name appears on the guest list. Emotional beat: the first crack in her picture of her own childhood.

chapters.title: The Cipher's Grammar
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Working from Tomas's notes, Petra cracks the cipher's structure: a notary's shorthand keyed to a family Bible in the Aldous house. The decoded fragments reference 'the payment' and 'the one who kept the books' — her mother. Meanwhile Halloran charges her with obstruction. Emotional beat: obsession as shelter from grief.

chapters.title: The Survivors' Club
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra interviews the three living fire survivors: patriarch's daughter Constance Aldous, now a beloved philanthropist; gardener Ivo Brandt, dying and bitter; and a nun who refuses to speak. Each gives the same rehearsed story — but Ivo lets slip that there were five people in the house that night, not four. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing a whole town conspired in memory.

chapters.title: What the Mother Kept
chapters.summary: POV Petra. In her mother's sealed estate box, Petra finds the cipher key and a ledger of payments from the Aldous family — thirty years of hush money that paid for Petra's education, her office, her life. The 'witness's closet' theft now makes sense: the framer knew the ledger's contents. Emotional beat: grief curdling into rage at the price of her own survival.

chapters.title: Constance Offers a Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Constance Aldous invites Petra to the estate and offers to make the charges vanish, fund her career, and bury the will — in exchange for the cipher key. She admits the fire was set to kill Elena, who was blackmailing the family, but insists Petra's mother acted to protect her child. Petra refuses and walks out knowing she's marked. Emotional beat: temptation met and declined.

chapters.title: The Fifth Person
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Following Ivo's clue, Petra finds the fifth witness: Elena's daughter, living under another name, who has been framing Petra to force the case into open court — the only arena where the family's power fails. She didn't kill Tomas; Constance's lawyer did. She gives Petra the final cipher fragment and a choice: testify or disappear. Emotional beat: enemy revealed as the only honest ally.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: POV Petra, climax at the trial. On the stand, Petra decodes the will aloud: Elena's confession, the family's crimes, and the ledger of everyone bought — ending with Petra's mother and Petra herself as beneficiary. Constance's counsel moves to suppress it; Halloran, finally convinced, arrests the lawyer for Tomas's murder as Constance's empire begins to collapse in the gallery. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into testimony.

chapters.title: Belonging to the Truth
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Weeks later: the charges dropped, the inheritance renounced, Constance awaiting trial. Petra meets Elena's daughter at the restored Varga grave and returns the ledger to the town archive, unsealed. She takes on a new client — a nobody with a contested will — and for the first time the work feels like a calling rather than a performance. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won belonging.
